# Results — Study 710 (Olympic-Host-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
HOST country's stock market rallies around its own Summer Olympics**, national pride and
an infrastructure boom lifting the host's equity market in the window investors actually
talk about. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Headline
panel fingerprint `c20a7e16e682`; per-ticker data fingerprints below.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes for six host-country ETFs — EWA, FXI, EWU, EWZ, EWJ, EWQ — and daily ^GSPC (price-only), 1998-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Host calendar | **hardcoded** table of **7 Summer Olympics editions** 2000 → 2024 (IOC results archive; opening/closing-ceremony dates) |
| Real-tape panel | **n = 6 of 7 hosts** — Athens 2004 excluded, no contemporaneous Greece ETF existed (GREK launched 2011-12-08, 7 years after the Games) |
| Benchmark | **^GSPC**, a named substitute for URTH/ACWI — both launch too late to cover the full 2000→2024 sample (URTH 2012-01-04, ACWI 2008-03-26, the latter landing *inside* the Beijing 2008 window). Host return is **total-return** (dividends included); benchmark is **price-only** — labelled everywhere it appears |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* (planned primary, n = 6 non-overlapping events) + median + **Wilcoxon signed-rank** (nonparametric cross-check) + **percentile bootstrap CI** (20,000 resamples) + a **random-window placebo** (20 seeds × 500 draws, matched trading-day window length per ticker) |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: enter at the **window-start trading day's close**, exit at the **window-end trading day's close** — host cities are awarded 7–9 years ahead, zero look-ahead |
| Data quirks (named) | **Beijing 2008** sits inside the Global Financial Crisis (Lehman failed 2008-09-15, inside this window's post-Games leg) — a severe confounder. **Rio 2016** coincides with Brazil's rebound off the January-2016 commodity-bust trough — plausibly the dominant driver of that number, not the Games. **Tokyo 2020** Games were held in 2021 (COVID-19 postponement); the window uses the actual 2021 dates |
| Data fingerprints | EWA `ed949ff1668d` · FXI `d95831e82b04` · EWU `739e7526d266` · EWZ `e45555abf3e0` · EWJ `80aff2dfb811` · EWQ `43d699436afa` · ^GSPC `1ed0e14c16a4` |

No survivorship on the Signal axis in the usual index-panel sense — these are six fixed,
named single-country ETFs, not a current-membership basket — but the panel itself is
necessarily small and hand-picked to the countries that happened to host, which is the
point of the tiny-n discipline below.

## The headline — host-vs-benchmark abnormal return, [-6mo..+2mo] around the Games

| year | host | ticker | entry | exit | host return | benchmark (^GSPC) return | abnormal return |
|---|---|---|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2000 | Sydney (AUS) | EWA | 2000-03-15 | 2000-12-01 | −6.57% | −5.52% | **−1.04%** |
| 2008 | Beijing (CHN) | FXI | 2008-02-08 | 2008-10-24 | −53.56% | −34.14% | **−19.42%** |
| 2012 | London (GBR) | EWU | 2012-01-27 | 2012-10-12 | +6.27% | +8.53% | **−2.26%** |
| 2016 | Rio de Janeiro (BRA) | EWZ | 2016-02-05 | 2016-10-21 | +89.68% | +13.89% | **+75.79%** |
| 2021 | Tokyo (JPN) | EWJ | 2021-01-25 | 2021-10-08 | −1.65% | +13.90% | **−15.56%** |
| 2024 | Paris (FRA) | EWQ | 2024-01-26 | 2024-10-11 | +3.15% | +18.89% | **−15.74%** |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| n | **6** |
| mean abnormal return | **+3.63%** |
| median abnormal return | **−8.91%** |
| sd (cross-host) | 36.16% |
| one-sample *t* (df = 5) | **+0.246** |
| two-sided *p* | 0.8156 |
| Wilcoxon signed-rank | stat = 6.00, *p* = 0.4375 |
| percentile bootstrap 95% CI on the mean | **[−15.13%, +34.11%]** (20,000 resamples) |

The mean is dragged from a deeply negative median into barely-positive territory by **one**
observation — Rio 2016 at +75.79 pp — out of six. Every inference method the desk uses at
this sample size agrees it's nothing: *t* = 0.25 is nowhere near the *t* ≥ 2 bar, the
nonparametric Wilcoxon (*p* = 0.44) doesn't lean on the one-sample-t's normality assumption
and still finds nothing, and the bootstrap CI spans **49 percentage points** and straddles
zero by a wide margin either side.

## Random-window placebo — is the observed mean unusual against *any* 6 random windows on these same tickers?

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed mean | +3.63% |
| placebo mean (20 seeds × 500 draws = 10,000) | +0.60% (sd 6.90%) |
| two-sided placebo *p* | **0.5950** |

Draw six random windows of the same trading-day length on the same six tickers, repeat
10,000 times: the observed +3.63% sits well inside the placebo cloud. Nothing about the
actual Games dates produces an unusual number on these tickers.

## Directional myth-check — does a MAJORITY of hosts actually outperform?

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| hosts that outperformed the benchmark | **1 / 6 = 16.7%** (Wilson 95% [3.0%, 56.4%]) |
| underperformed | Sydney, Beijing, London, Tokyo, Paris |
| outperformed | Rio de Janeiro |

If "national pride rally" were a real, broad-based force, most hosts should beat the
benchmark. Instead **five of six underperformed** — the positive headline mean is carried
entirely by one outlier plausibly explained by something else (Brazil's 2016 commodity
rebound, named above).

## Sensitivity cuts — transparency only, not a relabeling of the headline

| cut | n | mean | *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| excl. Beijing (named GFC confounder) | 5 | +8.24% | +0.48 | 0.6565 |
| excl. Beijing **and** Rio (named confounder + outlier) | 4 | **−8.65%** | **−2.14** | 0.1223 |

Dropping the two most-explained-away points flips the sign and pushes *t* past 2 — which is
exactly the shape of a **post-hoc, 2-of-6 cherry-pick**, not a second finding. It is reported
here as a warning about what selective trimming can manufacture at this sample size, not as
evidence for anything. (Note also its own *p* = 0.12 doesn't clear the bar either, at n = 4.)

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased, and the tiny-n bar itself is loose

Deterministic draws of *n* = 6 abnormal returns from Normal(effect, sd = 36.16, the real
panel's own calibrated dispersion); no network.

| world | outcome |
|---|---|
| null (effect = 0), **20 seeds** | mean *t* = **−0.30** (sd 1.48), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 3/20 seeds** |
| planted effect = +60 pp (seed 710) | mean **+44.33%**, *t* = **+3.96** |

The detector recovers a large planted effect cleanly. But note the null already fires
3/20 ≈ **15%** of the time at the *t* ≥ 2 threshold — because at **df = 5** the true
two-sided false-alarm rate of a fixed |*t*| ≥ 2 cutoff is **≈10.2%** (the actual 5%-level
critical value at df = 5 is 2.57, not 2). At this sample size the desk's usual bar is
*already loose*; that our real-tape *t* = 0.25 sits nowhere near even this weakened bar
makes the **None** call more decisive, not less. *(A faithful-engine / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

**Power curve** — fraction of 200 synthetic seeds firing |*t*| ≥ 2, by planted effect size:

| planted effect | +0pp | +10pp | +20pp | +30pp | +40pp | +60pp | +80pp |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| power | 11% | 18% | 37% | 56% | 76% | 97% | 100% |

Given the real panel's own dispersion, a TRUE average host effect would need to be roughly
**+30 to +40 percentage points** — an enormous, implausible number — before this study would
reliably detect it at n = 6. This is the honest power ceiling of a 6-event sample: the study
can rule out a large effect but cannot rule out a small-to-moderate one. Said plainly on the
verdict.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Mean abnormal return **+3.63%** (median **−8.91%**), one-sample
  *t* = **+0.25** (df = 5, *p* = 0.82), Wilcoxon *p* = 0.44, bootstrap 95% CI
  **[−15.1%, +34.1%]**, random-window placebo *p* = 0.60 — every method agrees there is
  nothing here. Only **1 of 6** hosts actually outperformed the benchmark (Wilson
  [3.0%, 56.4%]) — the headline mean is entirely an artifact of one outlier (Rio 2016,
  itself plausibly explained by Brazil's commodity-bust rebound, not the Games). n = 6 is
  tiny, said loudly, and the power analysis shows only a huge (≥30pp) true effect would
  have been detectable at all — an honest limitation, not license to round up.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** With no signal to trade there is nothing to size, and even
  setting the null result aside, the opportunity set is one non-overlapping 8-month window
  every ~4 years on a *different* single-country ETF each time — no capacity, no
  compounding, nothing a systematic book can be built around.
- **"Do most host countries actually outperform?" — BUSTED.** 5 of 6 hosts underperformed
  the world benchmark around their own Games; the "national pride rally" implies most
  should win, and instead most lost.
